title: The cost of cold
caption: The Carnot COP T_c/(T_h − T_c) means that removing 1 W at temperature T_c needs at least (300 − T_c)/T_c watts of work. At 77 K that is 2.9 W; at 4 K it is 74 W (COP 0.0135). Real refrigerators are far worse, needing about 1000 W per watt at 4 K.
alt: Minimum work per watt of heat removed against cold temperature from 3 to 100 kelvin: a curve that climbs steeply as the temperature falls, passing 2.9 at 77 K and 74 at 4 K.
description: Carnot: COP = T_c/(T_h − T_c) with T_h = 300 K, so work per watt removed = (T_h − T_c)/T_c.
T_c = 4 K: 296/4 = 74 W per watt, so COP ≈ 0.0135.
Real systems need about 1000 W/W at 4 K, far above this ideal limit.
